pr_title: Fix nested tag with "Ping-Pong" repeat mode causes to skip the first frame of the parent tag (fix #4271)
pr_body:
Issue #4271 has two issues (solved):
1. The nested tag with repeat mode "Ping-Pong" causes it to skip the first frame of the parent tag when it has to repeat the playback sequence.
2. Nested tag with "Ping-Pong" repeat mode causes to cancel the "Ping-Pong" sequence on its parent tag when it has to repeat the playback sequence.
And I found others (solved too):
3. Tag starting on frame 1 + "Ping-Pong Reverse" stops repeting the sequence on frame 1 when repeat = 1.
4. Tag starting on frame 1 + "Ping-Pong Reverse"  skips at least a sequence. For example: when repeat = 2 and aniDir = "Ping-Pong Reverse" the sequence is like aniDir = "Forward".
pr_comments:
@martincapello this fix solves only the "1". I will create other commits for the other 3 sub-issues.
EDIT: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/commit/0805df726fb02d7143446bfe9e3764bb132fd1e3 solves all cases.

Are items 3 and 4 actually issues? Because if you have a ping-pong reverse tag the playback goes backwards, so if you start at frame 1, you are starting at the end frame, then it immediately consumes a repeat.

> Are items 3 and 4 actually issues? Because if you have a ping-pong reverse tag the playback goes backwards, so if you start at frame 1, you are starting at the end frame, then it immediately consumes a repeat.

This is the issue "3":
![Mar-20-2024 18-03-32](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/32165475/0e526a7f-739c-40f3-abdf-d2f3fea669c1)

And this is the issue "4":
![Mar-20-2024 18-07-39](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/32165475/b4b18770-e596-40f3-be00-b48717e7253d)

Is this correct? Maybe I don't see that this behavior should be normal and that it solves other more complicated cases when there is nesting of tags. I'm not sure, I'm going to do some tests.

3. and 4. look like bugs. The correct ping-pong behavior can be viewed with a couple of extra frames outside the tag (here a video of ping-pong with repeat=2, ping-pong reverse with repeat=2, and then with repeat=1):

https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/39654/f06c5592-3c20-47b3-a4df-078a481d31bd

Just in case, for every bug that it's found it'd be nice to add an automated test to reproduce the bug/fix.
Thank you both for the videos! Now I see it.
@dacap you can review the tests added in `playback_tests.cpp`. I will try to improve the readability of the code in`playback.cpp`.
Ready for review. I'm not too happy with for loops, as they are probably harder to understand than individual cases.
I think I can squash all the code if you want.

issue_context.title: Nested tag with "Ping-Pong" repeat mode causes weird behaviors in Parent tag with any repeat mode
issue_context.body:
[Tag Repeat Bug.zip](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/files/13973733/Tag.Repeat.Bug.zip)

In the gif below, I have two animations built out of nested tags. In the first animation, both tags have "Forward" repeat. In the second animation, the parent tag has "Forward" repeat, while the nested tag has "Ping-Pong" repeat.

The first animation repeats correctly, but the second animation skips the first frame.
![2024-01-18 - 19-02-07](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/30498581/906fca60-8e0c-43dd-96d3-dbd983f627ba)

A Nested tag with "Ping-Pong" repeat will also cause a Parent tag with "Ping-Pong" or "Ping-Pong Reverse" repeat to break.
(Curiously, a Parent tag with "Reverse" repeat will play without issue.)

### Aseprite and System version
Aseprite v1.3.2-x64, Windows 11.
comments: Thanks for this report @HeyItsLollie! I was able to reproduce it easily thanks to your attachment.

review_comments: There is something about ping-pong cases that I'm not sure if the 0 of the last repeat should be merged with the 0 of the new loop (only when PlayInLoop). But I think we should keep the behavior as it's working. (Just a thought.)
Maybe it should be nice to have a checkbox to merge or not merge the last frame of a Ping Pong sequence. But for now it seems fine to me the way it is.
